text:
Maria: Heads-up — p95 tail jumped ~35% on the canary after last night's merge (commit abc123). Observed in our shortseq decode perf test (<=64 tokens). Starting a bisect, can we hold the rollout? :warning:

Alex: On it. Which path is regressing? shortseq or kv-warmup?

Maria: Shortseq decode + KV warmup interactions. Quick profiler snapshot shows attention choosing a fallback kernel for some shapes. Snippet:
```
kernel_selector.cpp:289 chooseKernelForShape(model=redwood/6B, seq=32): selected=attn_transpose (fallback), latency=1.33ms (was 0.78ms)
kv_cache.cpp:412 applyWarmup(): observed KV cache miss spike during prefix handling
```

Priya: CI perf also flagged this: `ci-bot` posted perf check failure at 03:12. p95 +28% on shortseq microbench.

ci-bot: PERF CHECK: shortseq_p95 baseline=0.75ms new=0.96ms delta=+28% (regression) — see http://ci/perf/6880012320

Sam: I ran a quick local repro with the canary build. When we force the kernel selector to prefer attn_matmul we don't see the spike. Suspect the fused-prefetch heuristic in PR 4587 changed kernel ranking for small seqs.

Jordan: Reproduce steps?

Sam: `bazel test //perf:shortseq_p95 --config=canary` then attach `--profile=kernel_selector` and look for `attn_transpose` hits. I attached a tiny flame excerpt: `attn_transpose` calls increased x3 during prefix path.

Alex: Opening bisect now. If it's PR 4587 that's the fused prefetch / batch steering change.

Maria: Can we hold the main rollout while we bisect? Deploy bot: can we pin canary?

deploy-bot: Recording rollout hold for deployment canary-2026-03-19. Traffic pinned to previous stable.

Priya: Running bisect: testing commits between stable (def987) and abc123. Will update every 10m.

(10m later)
Priya: Bisect update: narrowed down to 2 commits — abc123 (merge of PR 4587) and abc122 (related perf tweak). Running targeted tests.

Sam: I instrumented kernel selection to dump the ranking score. On abc123 we see fused-prefetch bumping `attn_transpose` score above `attn_matmul` for sequence <=48 on 6B. Score delta ~+0.4 which matches increased fallback.

Maria: Does reverting PR 4587 fix canary perf?

Sam: Local revert -> shortseq_p95 goes back to 0.76ms. Canary test with revert candidate `revert/4587` on a single machine showed p95 back to baseline.

Alex: Can we do a targeted revert of just the heuristic tweak (no large churn)? Patch idea: restore previous ranking weights for small seqs and add an explicit unit test.

Jordan: I'll draft a narrow revert PR and include the kernel-selector unit test and a perf CI guard.

Priya: CI perf run on revert candidate queued: `ci-bot` will post results.

ci-bot: PERF CHECK: shortseq_p95 baseline=0.75ms candidate=revert-4587=0.77ms delta=+2.6% (within noise) — full diff at http://ci/perf/6880012877

Maria: Good. Rollout hold can be lifted after we merge revert. Any other fallout? Did we see longseq changes?

Sam: Longseq unaffected. The fused-prefetch change improved some medium-length workloads, but regressions for shortseq outweigh that for now. Need a smarter conditional in the heuristic.

Alex: Action items:
- Jordan: open revert PR that reverts the scoring tweak, add unit + perf guard (PR 4592).
- Sam/Priya: produce reproducible perf test and kernel-selection dump script.
- Maria: coordinate rollback in console once 4592 merges.

Jordan: PR 4592 opened (narrow revert + test). @ci-bot please run perf.

ci-bot: Triggered perf suite for PR 4592.

(20m later)
ci-bot: PERF CHECK: PR 4592 shortseq_p95=0.75ms delta=0% — OK.

deploy-bot: Merged PR 4592 to main and triggered canary rollout (pinned traffic removed).

Maria: Monitoring canary now. Initial signs look stable. Thanks everyone for quick triage.

(1h later)
Maria: Canary p95 back to baseline across regions. Marking incident as resolved. We'll follow up with a postmortem + improved heuristics that are warmup-aware rather than global.

Alex: Postmortem volunteers: Sam, Priya, Jordan, Maria. I'll create the doc.

Sam: I'll work on a heuristic that inspects seq distribution and kv-warmup flags before bumping transpose score.

Priya: Adding a perf regression test for shortseq to run in our presubmit perf suite.

Maria: Closing thread. Reverting only the heuristic was the right call. Follow-ups tracked in #eng-runtime and the postmortem doc linked in the inc tracker. :white_check_mark:
